text: Fixed in src/interval.js: Interval.fromISO now catches the error thrown by DateTime.fromISO/Duration.fromISO when Settings.throwOnInvalid is true (previously the exception escaped instead of producing an invalid Interval), and the invalid explanation typo "asISO 8601" -> "as ISO 8601". Verified: Interval.fromISO("hello") throws with throwOnInvalid=true, and all existing interval tests still pass.

Fixed in src/impl/util.js: objToLocalTS re-applied the year with setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900), which left the month/day computed for the 19xx date (e.g. year 99 + 60 days landed in March instead of 0100-03-01). It now calls d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day), so calendar arithmetic across the 99/100 barrier (and leap-year differences) is correct. Verified against an independent reference for all months/durations 95-105; full suite still green.

Fixed in src/datetime.js: DateTime#isInDST compared the current offset only against January's and May's offsets, so years where the zone was on DST the whole time (e.g. USA 1974, DST from Jan 6 to Oct 27) reported false. It now compares the current offset against the smallest offset used in that year (the standard offset), so 1974 dates from Jan 6 to Oct 27 report true and the surrounding standard-time dates report false. Existing isInDST tests (pre/during/post DST, UTC, invalid) still pass.

Fixed in src/duration.js: the casual conversion matrix was missing years->quarters (4) and quarters->seconds (91*24*60*60), and the accurate matrix was missing years->quarters (4), so normalize()/shiftTo() produced NaN for those unit pairs (e.g. {years:1, quarters:1}, {quarters:1, seconds:1}). Added the missing entries; all unit pairs now normalize to finite values under both "casual" and "longterm" accuracy, and the duration tests still pass.

Fixed in src/impl/util.js: padStart ignored the sign of negative numbers, so toISODate()/toISO() for negative years produced "00-1-01-01" instead of "-0001-01-01". padStart now prefixes "-" and pads the absolute value (while keeping the previous non-truncating behavior for long values, so the existing "-118040-05-25" test still passes).

Fixed in src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js: isValid always returned true, so a FixedOffsetZone built from a non-numeric offset (e.g. FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp")) was considered valid and DateTimes in it were silently valid with NaN offsets. isValid now returns isNumber(this.fixed), so such zones are invalid and DateTimes using them become invalid ("unsupported zone"). Existing fixed-offset and zone tests still pass.
